identification: Box of three unframed prints: (1) Vanity Fair 'Men of the Day No. 1071' colour chromolithograph 'Jimmy' (golfer James Braid) by Spy (Sir Leslie Ward), published 26 June 1907, loose, shown on a pale mount; (2) a hand-coloured black-and-white Punch cartoon 'Quick Bridge' ('One Club, One Diamond, One Heart, One Moment') on a white mount, probably 1920s-30s; (3) a second Vanity Fair style colour print of a bearded academic in cap and gown holding a birch broom, in a mount in plastic wrap, caption not legible. Re-viewed all 4 photos at full size (small source images); cannot tell original from reproduction from the photos, though print 1 shows a printed Vanity Fair header and Spy monogram, consistent with the original plate.

viewing_check: Armitage estimate 30-50, current bid none shown (checked 9 Nov 2026), premium 22%, closes 11 Nov about 2:50 pm. The proper eBay sold evidence is now in: a genuine 1907 Braid print sold for A$13.53 plus postage (Oct 2026) and the larger Vanity Fair Supplement Braid for A$26.61 (Nov 2023); a multi-quantity reprint-style listing sold at A$9.53 each (Feb 2026). Other Spy golf prints sell A$37-80 each with outliers at A$145 (a lot of 3) and A$218 (Hutchinson, 'rare 1901'). So the dealer asking GBP295-425 is not what the market pays on eBay. Punch cartoons sell A$3-26 (sets cheap). Professor print: general Spy prints A$24-67 each, Australian subjects about A$26. Realistic value of the three prints is A$40-90 combined at best. Prices 2023-2026, steady. Andy should check whether the prints are originals (lithographic grain, original paper, Vanity Fair header/date), and condition (foxing, folds, trimmed margins). Not worth a bid over the estimate on this evidence.
